title: The Job-agent story
summary: A curated public playback of the current Job-agent product surfaces. It is not a reconstructed source-code history.
evidence_boundary: This story uses public, reviewed evidence only. The three interface frames are from the latest approved Job-agent iteration and use consistent synthetic placeholder data. They do not prove market validation.
evidence_gaps: The public record does not support finer-grained claims such as a first frontend launch or a complete frontend redesign history.
The public evidence shows application tailoring as a supported workflow output. It does not support a separate published personal-letter-writer feature claim.
The product surface is not evidence of live user usage, recruitment outcomes, or market validation.

events.title: Before build
events.summary: Job search was framed as a fragmented, context-heavy workflow rather than only a writing task.
events.how_it_works: The product scope connects opportunity discovery, career context, application support, research, and follow-up while the applicant retains control.
events.decision_annotation: Build a reviewed workflow, not a generic writer or an autonomous application sender.
events.why_it_matters: The product needed to reduce repeated context reconstruction without removing human judgment from sensitive career choices.
events.next_question: Which public product surface can make this connected workflow concrete?

events.title: Set up a repeatable way to find work
events.summary: Find jobs makes role criteria, sources, saved searches, and monitoring part of one visible discovery surface.
events.how_it_works: The applicant defines a search, reviews its criteria and sources, then retains a saved route for returning to relevant opportunities.
events.decision_annotation: Make discovery inspectable as a system rather than a single opaque search result.
events.why_it_matters: The interface shows how a repeated job-search activity can be organized before it becomes a one-off application task.
events.next_question: How should a discovered role move into a clear next action?

events.title: Turn the workflow into a daily next move
events.summary: Today gives the applicant a prioritised view of live work, filters, and the next move in the journey.
events.how_it_works: The surface combines the current journey position with a selected action and a filtered list of synthetic roles.
events.decision_annotation: Use a daily operating surface to make the next decision visible before asking the applicant to inspect every detail.
events.why_it_matters: It makes prioritization visible and gives the product a practical operating rhythm.
events.next_question: What evidence should be visible when the applicant inspects one role?

events.title: Bring fit, evidence, and action into one role view
events.summary: Job detail joins role fit, CV gap, company signals, and the next decision in the same reviewable surface.
events.how_it_works: The applicant can inspect a synthetic role with supporting signals and use that context to decide what to review or prepare next.
events.decision_annotation: Make the decision surface lead the public proof, with discovery and daily context supporting it.
events.why_it_matters: A recruiter can assess how the system moves from information to a human-reviewed choice.
events.next_question: Which public-safe evidence can test whether this decision context improves the workflow?
